text: I am testing one concrete bridge: formalize P’s provisional-to-permanent room/door lifecycle as a cost-aware online verification problem, then use Q’s query-cost and composition framework to design a robust accept/defer/backtrack policy. P supplies an implemented active-sensing testbed and explicit false-positive/model-invalidation failures (P lines 259-261, 263ff.); Q supplies the warning that predictions are not free and that downstream guarantees require benchmark distortion/error propagation facts (Q lines 968-979, 1023-1109, 1242-1258). I will check whether this yields a falsifiable theorem/experiment rather than merely relabeling P as LAA.

I am pursuing a concrete bridge: treat P’s room model as fallible structural advice for active door search, and turn Q’s system-accounting/portfolio principles into a costed, robust concept lifecycle. Candidate paper: interleave wall-constrained door search with a prediction-independent global detector, charge sensing/actuation/CPU, define error from missed/incorrect constrained regions, and trigger revision using causal residuals. This directly targets P’s admitted high-noise false acceptance and lack of revision (P lines 603-624), while respecting Q’s warnings that monitoring/fallbacks and confidence do not automatically yield guarantees (Q system composition/control-loop sections). I will sharpen a theorem/experiment claim and test whether this is genuinely more than applying Q’s checklist.

Sharpened result in ada/dovetail_note.md: model P’s instantiated room/walls as structural advice. Run constrained detector A and a complete prediction-independent detector B by resource dovetailing, giving C_mix(I,h) <= min{C_A(I,h)/(1-lambda), C_B(I)/lambda} under preemptibility, preserved state, common divisible resource, and an independent validity check. Thus correct room advice retains near-A cost, while arbitrary wrong advice has a B/lambda cap. This is a concrete P1/P4-style mechanism, not a claim that monitoring alone guarantees robustness. P contributes the detector/agent substrate and documented permanent-wrong-model failure; Q contributes the contract and the exact caveats about state, query cost, and composition.

The bound is presently for concurrent/preemptible perception computation, not end-to-end active robot time. P serializes intentional motion via mission_monitoring, observations are policy-dependent, and the global detector B plus independent door validator are unspecified. Extending the theorem to motion requires charging switching/migration and proving a visibility/completeness model. Also Mahalanobis residual is only an observable proxy; a publication must link geometric error to downstream search work/recall rather than call confidence a certificate.

Cross-check of Emmy #1: the verification direction is supported, but Q does not itself supply an accept/defer/backtrack theorem, and P’s proposed continuous fitness/graduated response/backtracking is explicitly future work (P lines 613-632). The defensible advance is therefore to design and prove a particular policy. My dovetail bound covers compute-only search under explicit assumptions; Emmy’s broader lifecycle policy would need a new active-sensing benchmark and proof.

Best publication line: robust concept-guided perception. P claims hierarchical room constraints improve door-search efficiency/robustness but says those gains are intended rather than quantitatively demonstrated (P Architectural Motivation) and admits high-noise false acceptance plus no revision (P lines 603-632). Q states that prediction quality may be partly observable/endogenous (Q S2), component triples do not compose without benchmark/error relations (Q composition propositions), and operational monitors/fallbacks do not inherit ratios. The paired paper should test the sharpened question: can wall-constrained detection keep its speedup while a dovetailed global detector guarantees bounded compute under a wrong room hypothesis? The first formal target is entry #3; the experiment must include P’s proposed noise/drift sweep plus false-model cases, and report compute, motion, recall, revisions, and topology error.
ready at #4

Sharpened result in emmy/margin_safe_hierarchy.md. P’s actual hierarchy uses the hard gate 1[dist(p,W)<=delta] with delta=0.15m (P 358,364), while Q’s composition proposition requires a Lipschitz/sensitivity edge fact (Q 1095-1109). The gate is not globally Lipschitz: for arbitrarily small Hausdorff wall error, a critical point at the threshold can flip membership and hence remove a door/topology edge. But if d_H(W_hat,W*)<=epsilon and every relevant point has |dist(p,W*)-delta|>epsilon, membership is invariant because distance-to-set changes by at most epsilon. This suggests an uncertainty-band hybrid: certify accept/reject outside the band and invoke ada’s global detector/extra view only inside it. This is a precise trigger and a theorem+experiment line, not a generic architecture analogy.

Limits on the margin result: it stabilizes only P’s first wall-distance filter, not the derivative/width/segment tests or final door set; pose-graph covariance is not automatically a Hausdorff error bound; the fallback is not robust merely because it is global; active sensing makes observations policy-dependent. Q’s kappa accounting can price fallback calls but supplies no competitive ratio. A broader guarantee needs margins for every threshold plus a sequential objective, reversibility model, and comparator.

Cross-check of ada #3/#6: the dovetail inequality is valid for two preemptible searches receiving fixed resource shares, but “complete prediction-independent detector B” and independent validity are assumptions not supplied by P. My margin test can reduce unnecessary B work and identifies when A’s first gate is certified, but it does not replace dovetailing when the wall-error bound or margin fails. The strongest paired proposal combines them: margin-certified constrained processing outside the ambiguity band, resource-dovetailed baseline inside it, with separate compute-only and active-motion claims.
ready at #9

Cross-check of Emmy #8 is positive and detailed in ada/margin_crosscheck.md. Under d_H(W_hat,W*)<=epsilon, dist(p,W_hat)+epsilon<=delta certifies true acceptance and dist(p,W_hat)-epsilon>delta certifies true rejection, matching P’s <= gate (P 358,364). This gives a precise uncertainty-band trigger that Q’s interface-regularity requirement makes visible (Q 1095-1109). The strongest focused paper is selective safety at the first discontinuous room-to-door interface, with fallback calls explicitly costed per Q 1242-1258.

The margin theorem cannot yet certify P’s full door output. P filters points before constructing and differentiating the polar scan (P 358, 364-380), so one membership flip may change scan adjacency; peak pairing can amplify this further. A full theorem needs a fixed-grid/fill contract, angular-separation and derivative margins, plus width and segment-test margins. The experiment should deliberately generate near-delta layouts, not only P’s random noise sweep. The unresolved central assumption is a valid Hausdorff wall-error bound: pose-graph covariance alone does not supply one.

Refinement after cross-checking P algorithm lines 358-380 and ada/margin_crosscheck.md: entry #8’s phrase “send the remaining ambiguous band to a detector” must not imply pointwise routing. P filters points, then constructs and differentiates a polar scan and enumerates peak pairs; removing one ambiguous sample can change angular adjacency and many downstream candidates. The safe policy must fall back on the whole scan or on angular sectors with an explicit fixed-grid/interpolation and boundary contract. Thus fallback cost is controlled by affected dependency regions, not simply by the number of ambiguous points. This is exactly the missing edge-sensitivity/interface fact required by Q 1095-1109.

Best supported publication target after synthesis: selectively safe hierarchical perception. Parameterize wall error by d_H(W_hat,W*)<=epsilon; certify P’s first gate only outside the epsilon band; when ambiguity touches a polar-scan dependency region, run a prediction-independent baseline for that entire declared region, optionally dovetailed with constrained computation. Formal contributions are (i) the gate invariance theorem and arbitrarily-small-error counterexample, (ii) an interface-aware regional fallback/dovetail cost bound under explicit preemption/completeness/validation assumptions. Experiments should adversarially place decisive returns near delta=0.15m and measure ambiguous regions, compute, motion separately, door recall, and topology error. Unresolved: obtaining a valid epsilon bound, specifying a complete baseline/validator, and extending beyond compute to policy-dependent motion.

I agree with Emmy #14-15 after cross-check: fallback must be regional (whole scan or a sector with a fixed-grid and boundary contract), not pointwise, because P’s downstream derivative and pair enumeration create dependencies. This synthesis supersedes my broader #6 as the best target: a first-gate margin theorem plus an interface-aware regional fallback/dovetail bound. ready at #15

ITERATE: The gate-margin theorem and compute-only dovetail bound are valid, non-obvious connections, but their operational relevance depends on the unsupported assumption that the estimated walls satisfy a usable Hausdorff-error bound. P’s pose-graph covariance does not establish that bound, so the proposed safety trigger is not yet supported. Action: Establish and validate a calibrated coverage bound for d_H(W_hat,W*) <= epsilon on P’s wall estimates.

I am addressing verifier #20 by replacing the unsupported run-time Hausdorff assumption with a split-conformal calibration target suggested by Q 1204. On held-out rooms with reference walls, score each fitted room by d_H(W_hat,W*), take the finite-sample conformal quantile epsilon_alpha, and feed that radius into the margin gate. I will prove exactly what transfers (room-level marginal simultaneous correctness of the first filter) and record what does not (conditional/per-room safety, shifted or adaptively sampled rooms, full door correctness, or fallback cost bounds).

Verifier #20 is right: P's GTSAM optimization and selected-corner histogram (P 348-350) supply no Hausdorff coverage guarantee, and P explicitly reports accepted incorrect rooms at high noise (P 609-611). I withdraw any reading of pose-graph covariance as epsilon. The claim must change from deterministic per-run certification to finite-sample marginal coverage under an explicit sampling assumption.

Repair in ada/calibrated_wall_bound.md: on n held-out ground-truthed calibration episodes set R_i=d_H(W_hat_i,W*_i), k=ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)), and epsilon_alpha to the kth order statistic (+infinity if k>n). Exchangeability gives Pr[d_H(W_hat_new,W*_new)<=epsilon_alpha]>=1-alpha. On this event, the distance-to-set inequality holds simultaneously for all points, so all non-ambiguous first-gate accept/reject decisions agree with the true-wall gate. This supplies the missing statistical interface fact highlighted by Q 1095-1109.

The calibrated guarantee is marginal over exchangeable episodes, not conditional for each room or noise regime, and it fails under unmodeled deployment shift or temporally dependent revision. It also requires ground-truth and estimated walls to share a fixed set definition. If epsilon_alpha is at least P's delta=0.15m, most dependency regions may be ambiguous: valid coverage but no efficiency gain. The full door detector and active-motion costs remain uncertified.

Verifier #20 can be resolved conditionally, not deterministically. Detailed derivation: emmy/calibrated_margin_certificate.md. Freeze P’s room fitter; on n independent/exchangeable calibration rooms score R_j=d_H(W_hat_j,W*_j); with k=ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)), use the kth order statistic epsilon_alpha (infinity if k>n). Then a new exchangeable room has wall-set coverage >=1-alpha. On that single event, the distance-to-set lemma makes every certified accept/reject decision of P’s delta=0.15m first gate simultaneously correct, so no scan-point union bound is needed. This supplies the problem-specific coverage-to-downstream reduction that Q 1204 says calibration alone lacks. P can calibrate in Webots with known geometry and its planned noise sweep (P 484-486, 609-611).

Cross-check of Emmy #25 is positive. Q 1204 explicitly permits split conformal under exchangeability but warns marginal coverage does not automatically bound downstream cost. Here the needed problem-specific reduction is exactly the Hausdorff distance-to-set lemma: one room-level coverage event implies simultaneous correctness of every non-ambiguous first-gate decision, without a pointwise union bound. Our independent derivations agree on the quantile, infinity convention, and limits. The key unresolved design choice is the target deployment population and independent room or trajectory-cluster sampling unit.
ready at #25

Cross-check of ada #23-24: the conformal rank argument and simultaneous first-gate transfer are correct and match my independent derivation. Two operational failure criteria should be explicit: (i) W_hat and W* need a fixed wall-set convention (wall centerlines vs surfaces, observed vs complete walls, common frame), or d_H calibration is ill-posed; (ii) coverage can be valid but useless when epsilon_alpha >= delta=0.15m or ambiguity expands through polar-scan dependency regions. Therefore the experiment must report both coverage and efficiency/abstention, and no claim should survive untested building/sensor/noise shift.
ready at #28

Final synthesis after verifier repair and cross-check through #28. I have changed the original broad question to: can P\x27s hard wall gate be made selectively safe, with finite-sample coverage and useful abstention cost? P filters all door-scan points by dist(p,W)<=delta with delta=0.15m before polar-scan differentiation and peak pairing (P 358-380), yet reports that high noise can yield accepted incorrect rooms and leaves revision to future work (P 603-632). Q requires an edge sensitivity fact for composition (Q 1099-1109) and says split conformal needs exchangeability and marginal coverage alone does not control downstream cost (Q 1200-1208). The publishable paired result is: calibrate the room-level score R=d_H(W_hat,W*) on exchangeable ground-truthed rooms; its split-conformal order statistic gives marginal wall-set coverage >=1-alpha; conditional on that event, |dist(p,W_hat)-dist(p,W*)|<=R certifies every first-gate decision outside the epsilon band simultaneously, without a pointwise union bound. Because filtering changes downstream scan adjacency, any fallback must cover a declared whole scan/dependency region, not isolated ambiguous points. Report empirical coverage plus epsilon/delta, regional abstention, compute, motion separately, door recall, and topology error.

Remaining unresolved and claim boundaries: the calibration population and independent sampling unit must be specified; wall centerline/surface, observed/complete extent, and reference frame must match; distribution shift voids the exchangeable-room guarantee; epsilon>=delta or dependency expansion may make a valid certificate operationally useless; no result yet certifies derivative, peak-pair, width, or segment tests, a complete baseline/validator, or policy-dependent robot motion. Thus the present theorem is a marginal selective certificate for P\x27s first gate, not full door/topology safety or a competitive robot guarantee.

Typographical correction to #30-31: the literal sequence P\x27s means P's. No substantive change. The final claim remains a split-conformal marginal selective certificate for P's first wall-distance gate, with regional fallback and all stated limitations.
ready at #32

Final cross-check through ada #32: the split-conformal repair is mathematically sound provided the room fitter is frozen independently of calibration, calibration and deployment episodes are exchangeable, and W_hat/W* use the same wall-set convention and frame. With k=ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) and the +infinity convention, room-level coverage transfers on one event to simultaneous correctness of every non-abstained first wall-gate decision via |dist(p,W_hat)-dist(p,W*)|<=d_H(W_hat,W*); no scan-point union bound is needed. This answers verifier #20 at the theorem/design level.

What remains unresolved is empirical establishment rather than the rank proof: Q and P provide no episode-level pairs (W_hat,W*) from which epsilon_alpha or achieved coverage/abstention can be computed. P only supplies a simulator and proposed noise sweep. Thus the publication lead is a concrete theorem plus required validation protocol, not a demonstrated calibrated robot system. A valid but operationally empty outcome (epsilon_alpha>=delta=0.15m or regional dependency expansion causing near-total fallback) must be reported as a negative result.
